benchmark: Economic OS to OCEL 2.0 loss-aware crosswalk
canonical_source: FIN-EFFECT owner effects plus domain-owned source records and explicit causal references
stable_rules: OCEL is a derived analytical view; it is never the canonical journal or authority system.
Each OCEL event requires a qualified source event-time assertion; record-time, ingestion-time and sequence numbers are not substitute event times.
Every exported event carries source_time_basis and time_evidence_ref attributes in addition to the OCEL time field.
Object attribute values carry their own OCEL time and source_time_basis/time_evidence_ref attributes.
The FIN/SAP causal graph remains a separate owner-scoped sidecar; OCEL event-object and object-object relations do not encode event-event happens-before.
Owner, authority, legal title, beneficiary receipt and settlement claims require their own evidence profiles; object co-occurrence never grants them.
Unsupported or excluded source fields must appear in the loss manifest; silent omission is rejected.

object_types.name: EconomicObligation
object_types.non_equivalence: Stable identity is not authority or proof of discharge.

object_types.name: GrantAllocation
object_types.non_equivalence: Approval and reservation are separate from tranche release and recipient claim.

object_types.name: PurchaseOrder
object_types.non_equivalence: Order commitment is not goods receipt or supplier acceptance.

object_types.name: Supplier
object_types.non_equivalence: Supplier object identity does not prove legitimacy or mandate.

object_types.name: DeliveryLot
object_types.non_equivalence: Dispatch and visibility are not beneficiary acceptance or quality certification.

object_types.name: Beneficiary
object_types.non_equivalence: A beneficiary object is not an entitlement or receipt claim.

object_types.name: Invoice
object_types.non_equivalence: Invoice validity is not goods receipt or payment.

object_types.name: Payable
object_types.non_equivalence: A payable is not an external payment instruction or settlement.

object_types.name: PaymentInstruction
object_types.non_equivalence: Instruction and provider acceptance are not bank settlement.

object_types.name: TreasuryOwner
object_types.non_equivalence: Treasury observation cannot write or assert another owner's effect.

object_types.name: ExternalAccount
object_types.non_equivalence: An account statement entry is an observation under a bank profile, not universal legal finality.

event_types.name: beneficiary_accepted
event_types.claim_ceiling: beneficiary acceptance assertion supported within named profile

event_types.name: provider_status_observed
event_types.claim_ceiling: provider status observed under provider profile

event_types.name: statement_entry_observed
event_types.claim_ceiling: statement entry observed from named external account source

relationship_qualifiers.name: obligation_for
relationship_qualifiers.meaning: source order references the named obligation

relationship_qualifiers.name: supplier_for_order
relationship_qualifiers.meaning: source contract or order names supplier

relationship_qualifiers.name: lot_for_order
relationship_qualifiers.meaning: source shipping/receipt record binds lot to order

relationship_qualifiers.name: instruction_to_supplier
relationship_qualifiers.meaning: payment beneficiary/payee relationship as declared by instruction

relationship_qualifiers.name: statement_for_instruction
relationship_qualifiers.meaning: statement source correlates entry to instruction

rejected_promotions.reason: Attribution is not legal authority or scoped delegation.
Visibility is not beneficiary acceptance or title transfer.

rejected_promotions.from: ISO 20022 pain.001 or generic pacs.002 status
rejected_promotions.reason: Instruction and status semantics depend on rail-specific evidence and finality profile.
Invoice conformance does not prove physical delivery or supplier authority.
A qualified analytical relation is not a legal ownership or authorization proof.
